questions.q: What is the word equation for photosynthesis?
a: Carbon dioxide + water ---> glucose + oxygen (in the presence of light and chlorophyll)
Glucose + oxygen ---> carbon dioxide + water + energy

Why do plants store carbohydrates as starch rather than as glucose?
a: Starch is a gas that escapes through leaves
Glucose is too complex to store
Starch is insoluble and osmotically inactive, whereas glucose is soluble and would affect water potential

questions.q: Which layer of a leaf contains the highest concentration of chloroplasts for maximum light absorption?
What is the role of the waxy cuticle on the upper epidermis of a leaf?
a: To absorb sunlight for dark reactions
To reduce water loss by evaporation from the leaf surface
To allow rapid entry of carbon dioxide gas

questions.q: How do carbon dioxide molecules enter a leaf during photosynthesis?
a: Through active transport in root hair cells
Through microscopic pores called stomata by diffusion
Through xylem vessels from the roots

questions.q: What factor is described as 'the factor that is present in the shortest supply and restricts the rate of photosynthesis'?
What happens to the rate of photosynthesis as light intensity increases from zero up to a certain point?
a: The rate increases proportionally up to a point where another factor becomes limiting
The rate decreases immediately due to bleaching
The rate remains completely flat and unaffected

questions.q: Why do plants require mineral ions such as magnesium?
a: To manufacture the central magnesium ion component of chlorophyll molecules
To maintain turgor pressure in vacuoles
To form amino acid peptide bonds

questions.q: What deficiency symptom typically appears in a plant lacking sufficient nitrate ions?
a: Stunted growth and yellowing of older leaves due to a lack of amino acid and protein synthesis
White spots on the leaf cuticle

questions.q: What is the primary function of spongy mesophyll cells in a leaf?
a: To form a rigid waterproof barrier
To carry out primary transpiration pull
To absorb mineral ions from rainwater
To provide air spaces that facilitate the rapid diffusion of carbon dioxide and oxygen inside the leaf

questions.q: What role do guard cells play in controlling gas exchange?
a: They change shape to open and close stomata, regulating gas diffusion and water vapor loss
They synthesize glucose in the dark
They transport water up the stem

questions.q: How does temperature affect the rate of photosynthesis?
a: Higher temperatures always increase photosynthesis infinitely
As temperature rises toward an optimum, photosynthetic enzymes work faster, but temperatures above optimum denature enzymes and drop the rate
Temperature has no impact on photosynthesis
Cold temperatures speed up light-dependent reactions

questions.q: Why is sodium hydrogen carbonate (or carbon dioxide gas) added to water plant experiments when measuring oxygen production?
a: To provide a ready source of dissolved carbon dioxide for photosynthesis

questions.q: What is formed when glucose produced during photosynthesis is converted for transport through the phloem?
Which of the following describes the compensation point in plants?
a: The light intensity at which the rate of photosynthesis exactly equals the rate of respiration
The maximum possible rate of sugar production
The point where stomata close permanently

questions.q: Why are variegated leaves (having green and white patches) often used in experimental investigations of photosynthesis?
a: To prove that water is required for starch production
To demonstrate that chlorophyll is necessary for photosynthesis, as only the green parts produce starch
To show that carbon dioxide enters through veins

questions.q: What is the purpose of de-starching a plant by placing it in a dark cupboard for 48 hours prior to a photosynthesis experiment?
a: To ensure any existing starch in the leaves is used up and cleared so new starch production can be tested
To force stomata to open wide

questions.q: What chemical is used to decolorize leaves safely by dissolving chlorophyll during a starch test?
What is the final color change when iodine solution is added to a leaf that has tested positive for starch?
Which environmental factor is represented on the x-axis when plotting a standard graph showing light intensity versus rate of photosynthesis?
What happens when carbon dioxide concentration becomes extremely high in a greenhouse setting?
a: Photosynthesis rate increases up to a new saturation point where another factor (like light or temperature) becomes limiting

questions.q: Which of the following structures transports water from the roots to the leaf mesophyll cells to replace water lost in transpiration?
What is the primary gas released as a byproduct of photosynthesis?
Why do glasshouse commercial farmers artificially increase carbon dioxide levels and heating?
a: To maximize the rate of photosynthesis and crop yield

questions.q: How do guard cells become turgid to open stomata during daylight?
a: They lose all water by osmosis
They absorb sugars and mineral ions, lowering their water potential and causing water to enter by osmosis, making them curve open
They collapse inward due to heat
They seal the pore with a waxy plug

a: They lack nitrates for protein synthesis

questions.q: What is the role of the spongy mesophyll layer regarding gas exchange?
a: It prevents any gases from leaving the leaf
It produces oxygen via cellular respiration
It acts as a waterproof seal
It provides large intercellular air spaces for carbon dioxide to diffuse freely to palisade cells

questions.q: What causes stomata to close typically at night or during severe drought stress?
a: Guard cells lose water, become flaccid, and straighten, closing the pore
Carbon dioxide levels drop to zero

questions.q: What happens to the excess glucose synthesized in leaves that is not immediately used or stored as starch?

questions.q: Which of the following best defines an autotrophic organism?
a: An organism that manufactures its own complex organic food molecules from simple inorganic raw materials using light or chemical energy
An organism that feeds exclusively on other dead animals
An organism that absorbs pre-formed organic molecules

questions.q: What is the role of the upper epidermis in a leaf structure?
a: To provide a transparent, protective single layer of cells that lets light pass through to underlying tissues
To absorb mineral salts from air

questions.q: If a plant is kept in an environment with zero carbon dioxide, what will happen to its ability to produce starch?
a: It will produce starch twice as fast
Starch production will increase using nitrogen
Starch production will stop because carbon dioxide is an essential raw material for glucose synthesis
It will convert water directly into starch

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why photosynthetic rates level off at high light intensities?
a: The plant runs out of water
Chlorophyll molecules are destroyed by light
Another factor, such as carbon dioxide concentration or temperature, becomes the limiting factor
